claims.text: Laser-assisted machining with laser preheating and a TiAlN/SH-coated end mill will improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to conventional machining.
The proposed alloy contains titanium, nickel, and four other elements, with each constituent constrained to 5–35 at%.
Laser preheating should be adjusted to a near-surface annealing temperature.
The intervention will refine the near-surface grain size.
The intervention will reduce machining-induced near-surface defects.
The intervention will lower near-surface residual tensile stresses.
Laser preheating partially anneals the alloy surface during machining.
Laser preheating reduces thermal gradients during machining.
Reduced machining thermal gradients lower residual stresses.
The TiAlN/SH tool coating minimizes adhesion and tool wear.
The combination of laser preheating and the coated tool refines the surface grain structure.
The modified surface structure increases resistance to mechanical degradation at elevated temperatures.
Laser-assisted machined specimens will exhibit greater elevated-temperature creep resistance than conventionally machined specimens.
Laser-assisted machined specimens will exhibit higher elevated-temperature yield strength than conventionally machined specimens.
Laser-assisted machined specimens will exhibit greater elevated-temperature hardness than conventionally machined specimens.
Conventional machining produces higher residual stresses than the proposed laser-assisted route.
Conventional machining produces a less refined surface microstructure than the proposed laser-assisted route.
The benefit is limited to a laser-processing window that modifies the microstructure without causing adverse thermal damage or oxidation.
